winning_case.argument: Yes. Nobody else does what he does for his team, and I'd take him over almost every guard in the league.

royce.claim: Yes, Brunson is a top-10 player: he just won Finals MVP, and that is what top-10 means.
supports: Result and honor: NBA champion and 2026 Finals MVP, 3 All-Star picks (F4, F5, F6)
Image: a smaller guard who keeps getting to his spots, landed on his 25.6 a night (F7)
Turn Deacon's efficiency number: a shooting slump in 8 games is a small sample against a title run (F9, F11)
royce.answer: Concedes the 8-game efficiency is soft, says it is a small sample and the season-long record of awards is the bigger one.

deacon.claim: Not right now: this season his efficiency is ordinary and several guards clearly outproduce him, so he is top-15, not top-10.
supports: Rate stat: true shooting 53.8% and 41.4% from the field vs Luka at 68.5% and Shai at 55.8% (F9, F10, F41, F23)
Volume vs. others: 25.6 points and 5.1 assists vs Jokic's 9.3 assists and Luka's 38.5 and 8.0 (F7, F8, F34, F40, F42)
Availability: never played every game in five full seasons, 65 of 82 in 2024-25 (F3)
deacon.answer: Grants the Finals MVP is real, but says it is a result from last season and a team outcome, and the question says right now.

lonnie.claim: Yes, he is top-10 because of what he does for the Knicks: he is the engine of their offense and the scoring-and-playmaking combo is rare.
supports: Role and fit: very high scoring, high playmaking and high three-point volume, the profile of a lead guard (F7, F8)
Team context tied to what he does: Knicks +4.9 differential and tied for 5th in the East while he carries the ball (F14, F13)
Durability: 74 of 82 last season and 8 of 8 now vs Luka's calf year and 8 of 9 (F3, F37, F38)
lonnie.answer: Concedes Luka and Jokic are ahead of him, and says top-10 only needs him to be ahead of the field behind them.

beats: Opening positions: Deacon says top-15 on efficiency, Lonnie and Royce say top-10 on role and results
Main clash: this season's numbers vs. a title and a Finals MVP, and whose sample is small
Trap: Deacon is asked whether eight games or five seasons decides it; Royce is asked who he drops to make room
Decisive exchange: availability and the gap to the players ahead of him; Deacon's case gets pressed on using small-sample numbers

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: You're on the Sideline. Go ahead, Terrence from Albany.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Everybody in New York has crowned Jalen Brunson already. I don't buy it. Convince me he's a top-10 player right now.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Listen here, I'll tell you where I land. Not top-10, he's just outside it. Right now he's at 53.8 true shooting, that's scoring efficiency counting threes and free throws, and Luka's at 68.5. Shai's at 55.8. He's shooting 41.4 from the field. That's a lot of shots for that kind of return.

stat.label: Jalen Brunson · true shooting percentage
stat.definition: Scoring efficiency counting threes and free throws: points / (2 x (shots + 0.44 x free throws)), in percent.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Eight games, Deac. Eight. You're grading a whole season off a week and a half. What does the guy actually do for that team? He scores, he creates, he runs the point. That's a lead guard, and there aren't many who do both.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: And you want to talk about right now? Right now he's the Finals MVP. Champion. Three straight All-Star teams. To my eye, he's a guy who keeps getting where he wants to go against bigger defenders, and that's 25.6 a night. That's not a slump, that's a man who just won the whole thing.

stat.label: Jalen Brunson · NBA champion
stat.definition: From his Wikipedia page: NBA champion ()

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Okay, Deacon. You want him out of the top ten. Name who's ahead of him. Because I count Luka, Jokic, Shai. Who else?

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Don't dodge. Royce, that Finals MVP is last season. The question says right now. And it's a team outcome, he had help.

stat.label: Jalen Brunson · NBA Finals MVP
stat.definition: From his Wikipedia page: NBA Finals MVP (2026)

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Team outcome. Okay, I hear you. But voters picked him out of the whole roster, Deacon. And Lonnie just pointed out eight games is a small sample. Is it enough to drop him?

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: No. Fair, it's eight games, for me too. So I'll go bigger. In five full seasons he hasn't played every game once. 65 of 82 in 2024-25. A top-10 guy is out there.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Hold on. 74 of 82 last season. Eight for eight now. And Luka's the one who played 50 of 82 in 2024-25. Who's more available?

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Missed a quarter of the games in zero of five seasons? Okay. That's real. He's durable. I give you that.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: And you gave it up quick. So where's the case now?

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: The case is Jokic at 9.3 assists. Luka at 8. He's at 5.1. If you're elite, you create more than that. That's the playmaker bar.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: That's the bar for top-three. Is it the bar for ten? He's at 5.1 assists and scoring 25.6 on top of it. Who else in the league does both?

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Wait a second. Deacon, you're comparing him to Jokic, a center. Of course Jokic has more assists. That's a different job.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Same question, Royce. Who's better right now?

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Jokic. Luka. Shai. I said it. Brunson's fourth or fifth, so he's top-10. Easy.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: And the Knicks are plus 4.9 a game, tied for fifth in the East. He's the point guard on that team, so that tells you something. I'd say top-10. Nobody has named anyone ahead of him besides those three.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: A 4-4 team. That's the record, Lonnie. And what would change it? If his efficiency is still sitting where it is now a month from now, I'm right. If it climbs well past that by Christmas, I'm wrong.

stat.label: New York Knicks · record
stat.definition: Wins and losses this regular season.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: Final answers. One sentence each. Is he top-10?

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Not yet. The efficiency has to come up before I move him inside the ten.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Yes. A man who just won Finals MVP belongs in the top ten, and nobody in the building thinks otherwise.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Yes. Nobody else does what he does for his team, and I'd take him over almost every guard in the league.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: On the scorecard, tonight goes to Lonnie. He kept asking who was ahead of Brunson, and no one named anyone past Luka, Jokic and Shai, while he leaned on a Knicks team that is plus 4.9 a game with him at the point.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: That's the board. Thanks for the call, Terrence.
